nodes.label: CodeQL SAST Workflow
nodes.rationale: Repo is public so GitHub Advanced Security is free; findings go to Security > Code scanning tab and do not fail CI - to make them blocking, add the check to master branch protection.

nodes.label: Deploy Prod Workflow (protected production deploy)
nodes.rationale: Key differences vs deploy-dev by design: GitHub environment 'production' with required reviewers (manual approval before touching resources), *-prod-* Azure resources, immutable SHA-tagged images, backup/PITR verification BEFORE migrations, no demo seed (only idempotent base seed of roles/breeds), minReplicas=1 for web/api to avoid cold starts, mandatory mail secrets (API refuses to start without SMTP credentials).

nodes.label: PITR Backup Verification Step
nodes.rationale: In production, migrations must only run with active backups: the step fails the deploy if Postgres flexible-server backup retention is below 7 days or cannot be read.

nodes.label: Rollback Prod Workflow (image swap)
nodes.rationale: Application-level rollback only: swaps web/api/worker back to a previous SHA-tagged image already in ACR. It deliberately does NOT roll back database migrations - destructive migrations require a dedicated runbook (backup/restore or corrective migration); safe only with additive, backward-compatible migrations. Secrets, identity and env vars are left untouched.

nodes.label: Security Scanning Workflow
nodes.rationale: Account-free security scans: gitleaks secret scanning blocks on found secrets; Semgrep SAST (OWASP/CWE rules) uploads to the Security tab without blocking CI; pnpm audit is informational only. Blocking behavior is deferred to branch protection.

nodes.label: SAST Job (Semgrep OWASP Top Ten / CWE Top 25)
nodes.norm_label: sast job (semgrep owasp top ten / cwe top 25)

nodes.label: Azure Key Vault Runtime Secrets (DATABASE-URL, REDIS-URL, S3, MAIL-PASS)
nodes.norm_label: azure key vault runtime secrets (database-url, redis-url, s3, mail-pass)

nodes.label: Graphify Knowledge Graph Convention
nodes.rationale: Codebase questions should go through graphify query/path/explain against graphify-out/ first because they return a scoped subgraph much smaller than raw grep or the full graph report; the graph is kept current with AST-only updates after code changes.

nodes.label: Go-Live Checklist (COSE DA FARE PRE LOGIN)
nodes.rationale: The code is a technical release-candidate (~75% toward public MVP); what blocks go-live is almost never application code but three external integrations (email, phone, legal), prod infrastructure and legal compliance.
nodes.norm_label: go-live checklist (cose da fare pre login)

nodes.label: Real Email Provider (Resend/Brevo authenticated SMTP)
nodes.rationale: Named the single highest-impact first step: it alone unlocks email verification, password reset, contact forwarding and notifications. In production the app refuses to start if SMTP is localhost/smtp.invalid or credentials are missing - a deliberate gate.

nodes.label: PHONE_VERIFICATION_ENABLED Flag (email-only contact)
nodes.rationale: Deliberate choice: email-only contact now, SMS (Twilio Verify) later. With the flag off (default in prod) OTP endpoints return 503, the listing form hides the phone contact, and submit-for-review forces email contact so no unverified phone number is ever published.

nodes.label: Legal Pages + Cookie Banner (/privacy, /cookie, /termini)
nodes.rationale: GDPR draft texts shipped with in-page 'to be validated' notices; owner must have a consultant validate them and fill in data-controller placeholders before opening to the public.

nodes.label: Email Verification Gate on Publication
nodes.rationale: Deliberate trade-off for less friction: login stays free of email verification, but submitDraftForReview rejects when email_verified_at is null (no extra query - the field is read in the draft fetch). The web submit panel warns, disables submit and offers a resend-email button.

nodes.label: Active Session Management UI (list + selective revoke)
nodes.norm_label: active session management ui (list + selective revoke)

nodes.label: Google OAuth Login (Authorization Code + PKCE, flag-gated)
nodes.rationale: Scaffolded behind GOOGLE_OAUTH_ENABLED (off by default, endpoints return 503) because the real round-trip with Google cannot be tested without credentials. Flow: /auth/oauth/google/start (state+PKCE+nonce in Redis) -> callback (code exchange -> userinfo -> find-or-create user + identity in new oauth_identities table, session, one-time handoff) -> finish; web button gated by NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_OAUTH_ENABLED.
nodes.norm_label: google oauth login (authorization code + pkce, flag-gated)

nodes.label: GDPR Data Lifecycle (export + account deletion)
nodes.rationale: Data portability via GET /users/me/export and web download /api/account/export; right-to-erasure via DELETE me which anonymizes email/data and revokes sessions. Retention policy for logs/audit/backups still to be defined by owner/legal.

nodes.label: MFA for Admin/Moderator Roles
nodes.rationale: Code search for mfa/totp/2fa found no implementation although docs require MFA for internal roles; the fast no-code fix is Cloudflare Access + MFA on the admin domain, with app-level TOTP as an optional later step.

nodes.label: Real Observability (OpenTelemetry export, dashboards, alerts)
nodes.rationale: Needed because today health/metrics/alerts are only in-memory and local; plan is OTel export to Azure Monitor/Dynatrace with p95/p99 dashboards and alerts on 5xx, failed logins, anomalous 429s, worker queues and admin actions.

nodes.label: Domain + Cloudflare Edge (DNS/TLS for www, api, media, admin)
nodes.rationale: Dev currently runs on temporary Azure URLs + r2.dev; the adottaungatto.it domain and edge perimeter (including Cloudflare Access on admin) are not yet configured.
nodes.norm_label: domain + cloudflare edge (dns/tls for www, api, media, admin)

nodes.label: Backup / PITR + Tested Restore
nodes.rationale: Backups and PITR must be active in prod and a restore tested at least once, with a rollback runbook distinguishing app rollback from destructive-migration recovery.

nodes.label: Moderatori/Admin Persona
nodes.rationale: Every listing is reviewed by real people before publication; moderators work in dense, operational surfaces.

nodes.label: adottaungatto.it Marketplace Purpose
nodes.rationale: Italian marketplace for responsible cat adoption: geolocated and breed search, human-moderated listings, direct contact between adopter and lister without intermediaries. Success metric is a conscious adoption; the site must remain an operational marketplace, not a decorative landing page.

nodes.label: WCAG 2.1 AA Accessibility Standard
nodes.rationale: Contrast >= 4.5:1 for body text including accessible variants of logo colors (coral-strong/teal-strong for text and CTAs), visible focus, prefers-reduced-motion respected on every animation, touch targets >= 44px on mobile.

nodes.label: Next Steps Plan (remaining go-live tasks)
nodes.rationale: Companion of the go-live checklist that keeps only what is NOT yet done; recommended order: accounts/infra first (unblocks first real prod deploy), then legal before opening to public, then branch protection and blocking scans, then session UI/email gate, observability/DAST, and growth items last.

nodes.label: Azure Prod Infrastructure (rg/acr/kv/cae/identity/psql -prod-itn)
nodes.rationale: Required resources: rg-adotta-prod-itn, acradottaprod, kv-adotta-prod-itn, cae-adotta-prod-itn, id-adotta-prod-pull, psql-adotta-prod-itn; Postgres extensions postgis, pg_trgm, unaccent, pgcrypto, pg_stat_statements; plus network access to Postgres for migrations run from GitHub Actions.

nodes.label: GitHub Environment 'production' with Required Reviewers
nodes.rationale: Required reviewers on the GitHub environment is what enforces manual approval of production deploys; it also holds the OIDC secrets (AZURE_CLIENT_ID/TENANT_ID/SUBSCRIPTION_ID) and runtime vars (MAIL_*, S3_*, PHONE_VERIFICATION_ENABLED, TRUSTED_ACTION_ORIGINS, USE_CUSTOM_DOMAINS).

nodes.label: apps/worker (async jobs: media, geography, search benchmark)
nodes.norm_label: apps/worker (async jobs: media, geography, search benchmark)

nodes.label: pnpm release:check Gate (lint + typecheck + test + build)
nodes.norm_label: pnpm release:check gate (lint + typecheck + test + build)

nodes.label: Production Readiness Gates
nodes.rationale: Minimum go-live gates: green release:check, migrations verified in staging, green staging/post-deploy smoke, secrets kept out of the repository, real providers for database/Redis/mail/storage/observability, documented backup/restore and rollback. With APP_ENV=production the API refuses local configs like localhost, default MinIO or local bucket.

nodes.label: Wikimedia Commons (public domain / CC0 image source)
nodes.norm_label: wikimedia commons (public domain / cc0 image source)

nodes.label: ADR 0001 - Modular TypeScript Backend with NestJS
nodes.rationale: Single language across frontend, backend and worker; good testability via dependency injection; modular structure fits a wide domain and allows extracting modules into services later. Trade-offs: NestJS imposes structure/conventions and module boundaries require discipline.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0001 - modular typescript backend with nestjs

nodes.label: ADR 0002 - PostgreSQL, PostGIS and Initial Search
nodes.rationale: Less initial infrastructure, strong consistency between listings and search, good geographic query support, simpler local migrations/tests. Trade-offs: weaker ranking/typo tolerance than dedicated engines, index/query-plan attention needed; Typesense/Meilisearch/OpenSearch deferred to a later phase.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0002 - postgresql, postgis and initial search

nodes.label: PostgreSQL Full-Text Search with pg_trgm and unaccent
nodes.norm_label: postgresql full-text search with pg_trgm and unaccent

nodes.label: ADR 0003 - S3-Compatible Image Storage
nodes.rationale: No coupling to the application filesystem, stable contract between local and cloud, CDN-ready, simpler variants and lifecycle policies. Trade-offs: bucket/credential management, orphan file cleanup, requires a worker for robust processing.

nodes.label: Verifiable Local Demo Target
nodes.rationale: pnpm dev:demo + pnpm smoke:e2e must yield a navigable demo covering demo users in all roles, listings in all states, complete insertion flow, favorites toggle, account dashboard, correct authorization, real-time notifications and protected moderation without manual intervention.

nodes.label: Minimal Reading Rule for Agents
nodes.source_location: Lettura minima per ogni nuovo task
nodes.rationale: Reduce tokens and ambiguity: an agent must read only the documents listed for the active step, never all of docs/, and documentation tasks must not modify application code.

nodes.label: Modular Monolith First
nodes.rationale: A single modular backend is sufficient to start, simpler to test and easier to evolve than microservices.

nodes.label: Progressive Search Strategy
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL full-text, trigrams and PostGIS cover the initial phase; a dedicated search engine is added only when volumes or ranking require it.

nodes.label: Server-Side Permissions
nodes.rationale: The frontend is never the source of truth for roles, ownership or publication state.

nodes.label: Events and Queues for Slow Work
nodes.rationale: Geographic import, image processing, email, notifications and moderation checks run outside the request/response cycle via a separate worker.
nodes.norm_label: events and queues for slow work

nodes.label: Bearer Token Sessions
nodes.rationale: Initial sessions are bearer tokens stored hashed in the database, rotated after login and sensitive actions, revocable server-side, with absolute and inactivity expiry; HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite cookies planned for full browser sessions.

nodes.label: RBAC with Ownership Checks
nodes.rationale: RBAC for general roles (anonymous, registered, professional, moderator, admin) combined with per-resource ownership checks; every admin/moderator action generates an audit log.

nodes.label: Redis Fixed-Window Rate Limiting
nodes.rationale: Fixed windows with hashed application keys combine per-IP limits with per-email/token/user/operator limits; returns 429 with reason and retryAfterSeconds; RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED and multiplier env vars tune limits per environment without code changes.

nodes.label: Single-Use Hashed Tokens (Email Verification / Password Reset)
nodes.rationale: Tokens stored only as hashes, single-use, short-lived with configurable TTL; each new request invalidates previous unconsumed tokens; the reset request endpoint never reveals whether an email is registered; successful reset revokes all active sessions.
nodes.norm_label: single-use hashed tokens (email verification / password reset)

nodes.label: Privacy-First Contact Flow
nodes.rationale: Owner email/phone is never exposed; the requester email is used as Reply-To only after explicit consent, and the requester phone is shared only after a separate explicit consent and only if set in the profile; owners can disable contact per listing via contact_requests_enabled.

nodes.label: Database-Backed Contact Anti-Abuse Limits
nodes.rationale: Limits enforced on tracked records: max 1 request per user per listing per 24h, 5/hour and 20/24h per requester, 20/hour inbound per owner; exceeding a limit returns 429 with reason and retryAfterSeconds.

nodes.label: listings Table
nodes.rationale: Central listing entity with dual state machines: moderation_status (draft/pending_review/approved/rejected/suspended) and lifecycle_status (draft/published/expired/adopted/deleted), plus GiST location indexes and public filter indexes.

nodes.label: listing_search_documents Table
nodes.rationale: Denormalized table for public PostgreSQL search with GIN/GiST/btree indexes including geography expression indexes for distance queries; idempotent refresh is tied to moderation decisions, worker image processing and like/unlike.

nodes.label: Azure Italy North + Cloudflare Stack
nodes.rationale: Azure covers Key Vault, Container Apps, managed Postgres with PostGIS, an Italian region, OIDC with GitHub and future growth; Cloudflare reduces cost and risk on DNS/CDN/admin access, and R2 avoids egress costs on public assets.

nodes.label: dev-online Environment
nodes.rationale: Online developer environment close to production, deployed on merge to develop: synthetic/demo data only (never plain production dumps), developer allowlist or Cloudflare Access, same providers as production where cheap.

nodes.label: Protected Production Deploy
nodes.rationale: Production requires PR develop->master, manual approval on GitHub Environment production, backup/PITR verification, controlled migrations, post-deploy smoke and release annotation; destructive migrations must never be rolled back automatically.

nodes.label: Admin Host-Level Isolation
nodes.rationale: Admin/moderation is treated as an internal application: dedicated admin subdomain, Cloudflare Access with MFA and email allowlist, dedicated WAF/rate limits, noindex, short sessions; before public go-live /moderation must answer only from admin.* hosts while public domains return 404/403 or redirect.

nodes.label: Secrets via Key Vault and GitHub OIDC
nodes.rationale: Runtime secrets live in Azure Key Vault, pipelines authenticate via OIDC federated credentials instead of static cloud passwords, and secrets are never committed to the repository.
nodes.norm_label: secrets via key vault and github oidc

nodes.label: Idempotent Favorite Toggle
nodes.rationale: Adding requires a public listing and is idempotent; removal does not require the listing to still be public so users can clean up favorites left on suspended, expired or removed listings; UI uses a same-origin heart toggle without page redirect.

nodes.label: Warm Trust Visual Direction
nodes.rationale: Warm light surfaces with deep teal as primary, coral as emotional accent, amber and olive for highlights and states; exact logo colors are used only as accents because they lack contrast for small text on light backgrounds; the site must stay an operational marketplace, not a decorative landing page.

nodes.label: Global Brand Tokens in globals.css
nodes.rationale: Color tokens are defined once in packages/ui/src/styles/globals.css and mapped to shadcn semantic tokens; components must use semantic classes (bg-background, bg-primary, etc.) instead of raw colors.

nodes.label: Sample Page First, Approval-Gated Rollout
nodes.rationale: Implement only the home sample page first, stop, and require explicit user approval before applying the visual system site-wide, keeping the site usable at every step and avoiding an unreviewed mega-refactor. Phase 2 rollout was completed after approval on 13 May 2026.

nodes.label: Server-First Component Split
nodes.rationale: Pages, layouts and list/detail components stay Server Components; 'use client' only on small interactive leaves (forms, toggles, carousels); indexable public pages must be server-rendered and client components receive already-reduced serializable data.

nodes.label: Centralized Typed API Client
nodes.rationale: All fetch is centralized in apps/web/lib/api with env-based base URL, timeouts, typed error handling and UI-ready ApiResult.message without raw HTTP details; the browser never talks directly to the database or private storage, and bearer tokens are never exposed to the client.

nodes.label: SEO as Product Requirement
nodes.rationale: Metadata, canonical, sitemap, robots, JSON-LD and noindex rules are part of the product, not a final step; internal search filter combinations must not generate infinite indexable pages.

nodes.label: Presigned Upload Flow
nodes.rationale: The API checks permissions/limits, generates an unpredictable object key and a presigned PUT URL to MinIO; the client uploads then confirms; the API verifies the object exists before moving the record to processing - keeping uploads off the app filesystem, rate-limited per IP/user/resource and server-validated.

nodes.label: Image Status Lifecycle (uploaded/processing/ready/rejected)
nodes.rationale: Submit-to-review requires at least one ready image and blocks drafts with uploaded/processing images or unremoved rejected images, so only fully processed content reaches moderation.

nodes.label: WebP Variants (large/thumb) via Worker
nodes.rationale: The worker validates magic bytes, strips EXIF, recompresses and generates WebP large/thumb variants using the same random name in large/ and thumb/ folders; Content-Type is set by the worker only after validation.

nodes.label: ISTAT Official Sources
nodes.rationale: Only institutional sources (ISTAT codes, SITUAS, WGS84 boundary shapefiles) with checksummed import runs and valid_from/valid_to historicization, because municipalities change over time and imports must be repeatable and historicizable.

nodes.label: Staging to Promote Import Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Dry-run first (geo:import), idempotent staged writes deduplicated by checksum (geo:import:apply), diff-based transactional promotion (geo:promote / geo:promote:apply); repeating apply on the same staging produces no new inserts or closures.

nodes.label: ST_PointOnSurface Centroids
nodes.rationale: Centroids are computed with ST_PointOnSurface on the official ISTAT geometry validated by PostGIS so the point stays inside the polygon even for complex geometries; manual untracked coordinates are forbidden.

nodes.label: Aggregated Public Like Count
nodes.rationale: Public aggregated signal on published listings without exposing who liked; the public UI dropped the like gesture in favor of the favorites heart to avoid two similar actions, while like endpoints remain as a backend/search signal pending a decision on full removal.

nodes.label: pnpm dev:demo Bootstrap
nodes.rationale: Single recommended post-clone path: starts PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Redis, MinIO and Mailpit, waits for readiness, applies migrations, seeds base and demo fixtures, verifies large/thumb images in the local MinIO bucket, then starts pnpm dev; --reset wipes local Docker volumes first.

nodes.label: Local Demo Workflow (demo:setup / dev:demo / demo:fresh)
nodes.rationale: Single repeatable demo path so a new developer or agent reaches a local demo close to production; data resets must be explicit scripts limited to local services, never generic destructive repo resets.

nodes.label: External Service Mocks (Mailpit, MinIO, OAuth/moderation/payment adapters)
nodes.rationale: Mailpit mocks the transactional email provider and MinIO mocks S3; Google OAuth bypass only in local/test never production; moderation and payment providers stay behind mock adapters until a real provider is chosen.
nodes.norm_label: external service mocks (mailpit, minio, oauth/moderation/payment adapters)

nodes.label: Moderation vs Lifecycle Listing States
nodes.rationale: Moderation status (draft/pending_review/approved/rejected/suspended) is deliberately separated from lifecycle status (draft/published/expired/adopted/deleted); a listing is public only when approved AND published AND not expired AND not soft-deleted.

nodes.label: Pending Review Moderation Queue (/moderation, /moderation/queue)
nodes.rationale: Queue requires moderator/admin role, applies Redis rate limits, supports claim to avoid concurrent double decisions, and the frontend is server-rendered, noindex, inside a separate internal layout with authorization always enforced by the API (403).

nodes.label: Moderation Decisions (approve/reject/suspend, claim, comments)
nodes.rationale: Every decision requires a reason, is accepted only from the assigned moderator on claimed cases, closes linked reports (approve→dismissed, reject/suspend→resolved), sends opt-out-respecting emails, and always creates in-app notifications.

nodes.label: User Reports (POST /reports/listings/:listingId)
nodes.rationale: A new report opens or reuses an open case; if the same user already has a linked report on the same open case, the API returns the existing report instead of creating a duplicate to avoid noise.

nodes.label: Moderation Persistence (moderation_cases, moderation_actions, reports)
nodes.rationale: moderation_cases drives the operational queue, moderation_actions is the audit trail for open/assign/comment/report/decide; for production the audit must become immutable, searchable and linked to operational alerts.

nodes.label: Monorepo Layout (apps/web,api,worker + shared packages)
nodes.rationale: Structure hosts the required Next.js/shadcn monorepo plus backend, worker, shared packages and infra without premature complexity: packages/db is the sole owner of schema/migrations, packages/domain must be framework-free, packages/validation may depend on Zod but not NestJS/Next.js, infra/helm stays empty until Kubernetes is really needed.

nodes.label: In-App Notification Center (GET /notifications, unread-count, read endpoints)
nodes.rationale: Authenticated inbox for non-critical application events; email opt-out preferences never disable in-app notifications; the inbox stays the reliable source even when the real-time channel is unavailable.
nodes.norm_label: in-app notification center (get /notifications, unread-count, read endpoints)

nodes.label: SSE Real-Time Notification Channel (GET /notifications/stream)
nodes.rationale: SSE was chosen for local simplicity and compatibility with Next server-rendering; polling/server-rendered is only a resilience fallback. Current fan-out is in-memory in the API process, fine for single instance, but must be replaced/augmented with Redis Pub/Sub, Redis streams or a broker before scaling to multiple instances.

nodes.label: Notification Event Types (review submission, contact request, moderation decision, report decision)
nodes.norm_label: notification event types (review submission, contact request, moderation decision, report decision)

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry + Dynatrace Observability Strategy
nodes.rationale: Instrument with OpenTelemetry and send signals to Dynatrace, explicitly avoiding direct coupling of the observability vendor into the application domain.

nodes.label: Local Health/Metrics/Alerts Endpoints (/health/ready, /health/metrics, /health/alerts)
nodes.rationale: In-memory HTTP metrics and env-tunable local alert thresholds (OBSERVABILITY_ALERT_*) are a deliberate bridge toward provider-managed dashboards/alerts; the same signals must be exported via OpenTelemetry in staging/production.

nodes.label: Drizzle Migration Rules (additive-first, staged deploy)
nodes.rationale: Never modify released migrations; destructive migrations only with backfill and rollback plan; large tables use add-nullable/backfill/enforce phases; additive migrations must be applied before new API/worker versions that read those tables.

nodes.label: Release Gates (pnpm release:check, pnpm release:smoke)
nodes.rationale: release:check = lint+typecheck+test+build with no external deps; release:smoke = db:migrate + smoke:e2e against running local services; both must be green before any release, with migrations applied to staging first.

nodes.label: Security Posture and Pending Gates (MFA, scanning, GDPR)
nodes.norm_label: security posture and pending gates (mfa, scanning, gdpr)

nodes.label: Production Env Validation (loadApiEnv rejects local defaults)
nodes.rationale: loadApiEnv() rejects APP_ENV=production configurations pointing at localhost or using local MinIO/bucket defaults, so local credentials can never ship to production.
nodes.norm_label: production env validation (loadapienv rejects local defaults)

nodes.label: Project State Summary (14 May 2026)
nodes.rationale: Describes the real repository state, not the desired state; read before starting new development. New features must not be introduced without updating roadmap and area docs.

nodes.label: Milestone Roadmap (M0 foundations to M9 local product loop)
nodes.norm_label: milestone roadmap (m0 foundations to m9 local product loop)

nodes.label: PostgreSQL-First Search Strategy (tsvector, pg_trgm, PostGIS)
nodes.rationale: Use PostgreSQL as the first search engine because it reduces infrastructure, keeps consistency with the main database and is enough to validate the product; a dedicated engine (Typesense/Meilisearch/OpenSearch) only when latency targets, advanced ranking/typo needs or traffic justify separation.

nodes.label: Initial Search Ranking Formula (text 0.45 / distance 0.20 / freshness 0.15 / quality 0.12 / trust 0.05 / engagement 0.03)
nodes.rationale: Weights must become configurable after the first real-world tests.
nodes.norm_label: initial search ranking formula (text 0.45 / distance 0.20 / freshness 0.15 / quality 0.12 / trust 0.05 / engagement 0.03)

nodes.label: Empty Result Expansion Strategy (trigram, expanded_radius, relaxed_filters)
nodes.rationale: Every expansion must be declared in the API response meta so the frontend can explain to the user what changed instead of silently altering results.
nodes.norm_label: empty result expansion strategy (trigram, expanded_radius, relaxed_filters)

nodes.label: Local Search Benchmarks 10k/100k (8 May 2026, postgres-v1)
nodes.rationale: 100k queries stay under initial thresholds (filtered list <300ms, ranked q <500ms); results are indicative, dependent on local machine, DB cache and synthetic dataset; 1M limit test deferred until margin needs measuring.

nodes.label: Geography GiST Expression Indexes (migration 0013_elite_juggernaut.sql)
nodes.rationale: First smoke benchmark showed location_point::geography casts bypassed the existing geometric index causing sequential scans; migration 0013 adds GiST expression indexes on location_point::geography for listings and listing_search_documents, after which the geo plan uses a Bitmap Index Scan.

nodes.label: postgres-v1 Ranking (ts_rank_cd + distance + freshness + quality + trust + engagement)
nodes.rationale: text_score applies only when q is present; distance_score only with lat/lng within radiusKm; listings without a search document remain searchable via inline fallback but get 0 on non-textual boosts until document refresh.
nodes.norm_label: postgres-v1 ranking (ts_rank_cd + distance + freshness + quality + trust + engagement)

nodes.label: listing_search_documents Denormalized Search Table
nodes.rationale: A denormalized table is preferred over a materialized view in the initial phase to allow controlled refreshes from worker or application triggers; refresh hooks fire on moderation decisions, image processing and like/unlike.

nodes.label: Trigram Fallback for Empty Full-Text First Page
nodes.rationale: When q is present, page is 1 and full-text returns zero rows, a second pg_trgm similarity query runs with explicit filters unchanged, declared via meta.expansion type trigram_text / reason empty_full_text.
nodes.norm_label: trigram fallback for empty full-text first page

nodes.label: listing_promotions Declared Sponsored Slot
nodes.rationale: Active promotions never modify rankingVersion or the organic score: they occupy a declared slot ordered before organic results, and only when the promoted listing matches the applied filters.

nodes.label: Listing Quality Score (image/description/health-field weights)
nodes.rationale: The quality score is persisted in the search document to avoid heavy recomputation at query time.

nodes.label: Sponsored Listings Business Policy
nodes.rationale: This policy exists to prevent commercial logic from being introduced directly into the organic ranking without an explicit policy: sponsored listings must be recognizable, only approved+published listings can be promoted, moderation can suspend a sponsorship, spend must be auditable, and sponsorships should be implemented only after organic search, moderation and observability.

nodes.label: Dev-Online Environment (Azure Italy North + Cloudflare)
nodes.rationale: Container Apps, ACR, PostgreSQL, Key Vault and Redis on Azure Italy North with Cloudflare DNS/Access/R2; APP_ENV=production even in dev-online to exercise non-local cookies/headers/env validations; demo or synthetic data only, never production dumps; user handles logins/billing/DNS/secrets, agent automates the rest.

nodes.label: deploy-dev.yml GitHub Actions Workflow
nodes.rationale: Merge to develop is the standard trigger: build/push web+api+worker images to ACR, read runtime secrets from Key Vault, run migrations, optional demo seed, deploy Container Apps, then remote smoke.

nodes.label: Remote Smoke Script (pnpm smoke:remote)
nodes.rationale: release:smoke stays local-only; dev-online uses a separate remote smoke that checks health/readiness/listings/web pages without contacting Mailpit and without creating mutative data.

nodes.label: GitHub-to-Azure OIDC Federation
nodes.rationale: Federated credential scoped to the dev-online GitHub Environment lets Actions log into Azure without a client secret; minimal roles: Contributor on the resource group, AcrPush on the registry, Key Vault Secrets User on the vault.

nodes.label: Admin Host Guard for /moderation (ADMIN_ALLOWED_HOSTS)
nodes.rationale: In production-like environments the web proxy returns 404 for /moderation unless the request host is in ADMIN_ALLOWED_HOSTS (admin/admin-dev subdomains), hiding the internal area from the public domain.

nodes.label: geo:verify Italian Places Verification (evaluateItalianPlacesHealth, verifyItalianPlaces)
nodes.rationale: Worker command that fails when active places are incomplete or duplicated, so dev-online has the complete active Italian places dataset before demo data is seeded and developers can test any Italian municipality.

nodes.label: Deploy Workflow Places Guard (Ensure Italian places step)
nodes.rationale: Verification-first: run geo:verify before demo seed and only run geo:import:apply / geo:promote:apply / geo:boundaries:apply when verification fails, enforced by a regression test on deploy-dev.yml.
nodes.norm_label: deploy workflow places guard (ensure italian places step)

nodes.label: blur_data_url Design (new field, not blur_hash reuse)
nodes.rationale: Introduce an explicit blur_data_url field instead of reusing the existing blur_hash column: that name implies a different algorithm not directly compatible with next/image. If placeholder generation fails, the worker still produces large/thumb and leaves blur_data_url null.
nodes.norm_label: blur_data_url design (new field, not blur_hash reuse)

nodes.label: Classic Pagination Design Decision
nodes.rationale: Classic query-string pagination is preferred over infinite scroll because it is more readable, indexable, shareable and already supported by the API contract (page/pageSize/meta.totalPages).

nodes.label: Suggestions Separated From Exact Results Design
nodes.rationale: Existing fallbacks replaced the list when empty; the design instead keeps exact results in items/meta and adds a separate optional suggestions section with declared reasons, avoiding duplicates and never confusing alternatives with requested results. If only the suggestions query fails, log and respond without suggestions rather than failing the response.
nodes.norm_label: suggestions separated from exact results design

nodes.label: Cold Start Policy (dev-online minReplicas=0, production >=1)
nodes.rationale: dev-online may keep minReplicas=0 accepting cold starts to contain costs; production web and API must keep at least one warm replica; worker may stay at 0 if it only does controlled job/polling work.

nodes.label: Clean Marketplace Redesign (white + coral accent, Inter only)
nodes.rationale: The owner judged the editorial-pastel look unprofessional; move to an Airbnb/Idealista-style clean marketplace: dominant white, one coral accent, modern sans (Inter only), photos as protagonists, 3-column card grid, Airbnb-style detail with 2x2+4 gallery and sticky contact column, search-first hero.
nodes.norm_label: clean marketplace redesign (white + coral accent, inter only)

nodes.label: Warm Marketplace Redesign (V3 pulito minimal)
nodes.rationale: Replaces both the current editorial cream/terracotta tree and the pure white/zinc 2026-06-07 spec: warm brand marketplace with white base, warm ink foreground, logo palette as semantic accents (coral CTA, teal trust, olive free/success, amber sponsored), Plus Jakarta Sans for all product UI and Fraunces only in two brand moments (home hero H1, final CTA banner); photo-first because 'the photo is the conversion' in adoption marketplaces.

nodes.label: Brand Semantic Color System (coral/teal/olive/amber OKLCH tokens)
nodes.rationale: Raw logo colors only as graphic accents at >=3:1 context contrast, never small text; amber only as soft surface with dark text; warmth comes from warm ink, photos and accents, never cream backgrounds; contrast AA everywhere including text over hero scrim.
nodes.norm_label: brand semantic color system (coral/teal/olive/amber oklch tokens)

nodes.label: Demo Data and Fixture Contract (5 users, 15 listings, 11 assets)
nodes.rationale: Demo data must be idempotent; demo places must reference real imported places when they exist, DEMO-* records are only a minimal local fallback; no demo script may touch data outside local services; stable IDs preferred for tests and docs.
nodes.norm_label: demo data and fixture contract (5 users, 15 listings, 11 assets)

nodes.label: Demo Accounts (private, shelter, association, moderator, admin)
nodes.norm_label: demo accounts (private, shelter, association, moderator, admin)

nodes.label: Smoke E2E Coverage Targets (pnpm smoke:e2e)
nodes.rationale: Covers health/readiness, public search, auth, listing creation, image upload/processing, review submission, moderation approval, favorites, owner contact with consents, notifications including real-time SSE events without refresh, and multi-user isolation; falls back to the demo moderator when the admin login hits local rate limits.
